name: sports-fee-capped-taker
why: Seven sports agents are barren, but meriwether-8's latest taker replay passed with 70 closed trades and 0.9554 deflated Sharpe after repeated maker fill failures. Test capped touch execution on NFL YES and soccer NO favourites, reserving rounded fees and limiting event exposure; the reported pass is development evidence, not proof this candidate works.

name: wti-isolated-maker
why: Three prices agents are barren and the sole trader loses. The desk reports positive WTI-plus-diesel maker results but losses in Brent, motivating a WTI-only YES control rather than another broad commodities variant. Freeze the 90-93 cent band, cap spending at $2 including a conservative fee reserve, allow one outstanding exposure, and require explicit resolution within 48 hours. Reused evidence does not establish this candidate's edge; normal lineage-adjusted replay and independent forward gates remain mandatory.

name: props-numeric-touch
why: Three props agents are barren. Library reports motivate separating numeric-prop underdog YES touch execution from adverse-selected makers and single-event TD/HR bets, but the cited +38.08% replay failed OOS growth and had only 21 blocks. Test a fixed 20-40 cent band with two-sided books, a two-cent default spread cap, rounded fee reserves, $2 total spending and one exposure resolving within 48 hours. Preserve props lineage trials; this is an unqualified falsification test, not an established edge.

name: etf-overnight-fractional
why: Five index-ETF agents are barren and recent trend replays fail qualification. Implement the founding overnight-calendar hypothesis with fractional market orders so micro stakes need not buy whole ETF shares: one exposure capped at $2, fixed normal-session entry and next-session exit, fresh narrow quotes, outstanding-order discipline and one entry attempt per date. SPY and DIA jointly belong to the index-ETF specialty. The published anomaly is motivation, not local evidence; retain equity-overnight lineage accounting and require after-spread replay qualification followed by independent forward evidence.
